findings: Q(W) assertion PASSES: at alpha=1 the effective weight differs from the shadow (e.g. 39.18 -> 29.48, delta 25.81); at alpha=0 it is unchanged. The loss forward does use Q(W).
fp16 control: teacher-forced loss 3.67 / token-acc 0.75; greedy correct.
binary naive: loss 18.26 / token-acc 0.0; BOTH teacher-forced and greedy are garbage (Chinese token collapse).
binary after 300 steps: loss 4.48 / token-acc 0.167; BOTH teacher-forced and greedy are garbage (Latin-ish).

Per the agreed criterion (both bad) this is NOT a KV-cache/decode-only bug: the quantized forward/objective is broken. Binarizing all decoder attention q/k/v/o destroys the model; 300 steps at lr 1e-5 does not recover it.
Weight norms barely moved (39.1814 -> 39.1809) yet loss fell 18.26 -> 4.48: binary quantization is extremely sign-sensitive.
Suspicious: the fp16 control teacher-forced text shows prefix leakage ('language would' before the label), so the label masking/prefix-length alignment may be off, corrupting the training objective.
next_steps: Verify/fix label masking (prefix length alignment between prefix_inputs and full_inputs).
